description:
A GPU-accelerated terminal for Windows that keeps your sessions alive.

Nebula is a terminal emulator for Windows, built in Rust on a GPU-accelerated rendering core and designed around one idea: your terminal sessions are too valuable to die with a window. It pairs a tmux-style resident session model with a glass UI, an AI-CLI-aware sidebar, and a shell experience that works without extra setup.
macOS, Linux, and Android downloads are Preview builds.
Improved
- Improved tab recognition with a fixed icon before each title. Shell and tab type icons fill that spot by default, with activity still shown at the trailing edge. Addresses #871.
Fixed
- Fixed display formulas reverting to source when scrolled partly out of view and their source rows are still retained by the terminal. Addresses #909.
- Fixed LaTeX underbraces so they span the expression above them.
- Fixed annotated LaTeX arrows so their shafts extend to fit the labels.
- Fixed inline formulas ending at the right edge of a terminal row being rejected because of text on the next line. Addresses #772.
- Fixed empty command output streams so the stream switcher stays visible and copying leaves the clipboard intact. Addresses #900.
- Fixed directional pane shortcuts skipping the nearest pane when exiting zoom.
- Fixed shared Codex backends on Linux assigning a conversation to the wrong terminal pane. Addresses #633.
- Fixed Windows portable copies downloading a setup executable they cannot use. The update dialog offers the matching ZIP instead. Addresses #533.
- Fixed Android SSH reconnection opening a new workspace when the previous one has stopped. A running workspace still reconnects to the same shell. Addresses #794.
- Fixed the background color of opaque Sixel images when reverse video is active.
